comparison.extrapolation_scope: Linear estimate from a single two-minute excerpt; excludes decode, model preparation, validation, storage and Drive; not a measured full-episode runtime.

quality.quality_judgment: Unknown without an independent listening reference; text similarity is neither accuracy nor WER. Native token sequences and some token times differ despite identical VAD boundaries.
quality.listening_window_note: Source windows add the 300-second excerpt offset. Prioritize changed recognition; a simple token alignment can pair repeated subwords incorrectly and is not a timestamp ground truth.

report.conclusion: On this T4 and pinned runtime, the FP32 export removes the expensive encoder/decoder CPU integer path and improves median warm recognition speed 7.49-fold over INT8/CUDA on identical two-minute audio. This strongly supports the mixed INT8 CPU/CUDA execution path as the dominant performance problem in the tested configuration. It is not a complete device-time accounting or a full-episode/quality acceptance.
limits: Three samples per timing mode, one two-minute excerpt, fixed case order on one shared Colab VM.
Profiles use a separate eight-second prefix and do not measure profiling overhead on the timing excerpt. No Kernel-device events were captured; host duration sums may overlap.
CPU control has provider-dependent NumPy preprocessing instead of CUDA ONNX Conv; it is a complete-path comparison.
Model lookup/materialization and session construction are measured separately and excluded from the recognition medians.
No independent transcript or timing reference, full FP32 episode, long-session stability or peak VRAM proof was supplied.
Production settings and accepted transcripts were not changed by this evidence review.

measurement_gaps: The report contains no individual elapsed times for downloads, session creation, decoding, inference, validation, profile work or Drive copies; the operator supplied only the approximately 36-minute whole-cell boundary.
Audio SHA-256 and decoded duration are absent, so equivalence to the Windows CPU input is unverified.
The report contains no repository branch or commit, so code equivalence to the Windows CPU run is unverified.
The Drive profile files were not supplied with the report; node counts cannot establish time spent on either provider or transfer/synchronization costs.
The resume entry records a skip and runtime facts only; it does not include a second CLI run report or timing.
report.conclusion: The report proves that this Colab inference executed CUDA nodes and also executed CPU nodes. It does not reproduce or explain the reported 36-minute wall time. Node counts are not elapsed time, and no optimization conclusion is supported.

The historical Windows CPU input has different bytes and duration, and other comparison conditions differ; no valid historical CPU/GPU speed ratio.
The report was analyzed locally; the Colab GPU experiment was not rerun in this workspace.
Raw ORT traces were not supplied; analysis uses the report's aggregated trace summaries.

report.conclusion: Recognition dominates. Expensive INT8 operators demonstrably execute on CPU while CUDA executes other nodes; this is the strongest candidate for inefficient acceleration, not a quantified explanation of all wall time. Test the pinned unquantized FP32 export on the same short audio input before changing defaults or reprocessing full episodes.
